quote: Man is least himself when he talks in his own person. Give him a mask, and he will tell you the truth.
source: Oscar Wilde, The Critic as Artist, Part II, in Intentions, 1891 (Gilbert)
speaker: Gilbert

evidence.where: Wikisource text of Intentions, The Critic as Artist; a search of the page returns one hit, inside a long speech of Gilbert's that begins The difference between objective and subjective work, and the heading above it reads A DIALOGUE: Part II
evidence.edition: Intentions (Osgood, McIlvaine, 1891), The Critic as Artist, Part II
evidence.locator: Part II, closing the speech that ends the objective form is the most subjective in matter

reason: The two sentences are Wilde's own, consecutive and unaltered, and they sit in Part II of the dialogue in Gilbert's mouth, not Wilde's.
